scenario: [LFST.9.3.6]: a replayer compares `timetag` as an identity. It pairs each recorded `timetag` with the re-derived one the first time either occurs, and every later atom must agree with that pairing. [RFCS.11.2]: a `timetag` is stream-local, so two conforming engines may record different values for one run. The harness ([RCTS.1.2.24]) records two Trig asserts and a pump, so `seen` fires twice and each firing's RuleFireAnnotation carries a `timetag`, and then adds 1000 to every nonzero `timetag` in the recording (`timetag_offset`). Every recorded value now differs from the one the replay re-derives, but the pairing is a consistent renaming, so the replay must reproduce the run: no DS_ERR_FS_DIVERGENCE, the same facts at the end, and at least two rule fires compared. A replayer that compares the value byte for byte fails this vector at the first firing. PATHS: libds's `Engine.replay` in verify mode, whose `timetag` pairing is `rfcs/codec.c`'s; the Mercury runtime's `ds.replay`, which pairs a recorded `timetag` with the re-derived one at first occurrence.
